newsitem.title: UK: Anglo-French safety authority report due Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Anglo-French safety authority report due Tuesday.

text.p: The Anglo-French Channel Tunnel Safety Authority is due on Tuesday to publish its final report into last November's fire which swept through a main tunnel creating tens of millions of pounds of damage.
A spokesman for the British Department of Transport said the report would be published in London at 0930 GMT on Tuesday.
Eurotunnel Plc, the Channel Tunnel operator, recently said it was confident the CTSA report would clear the design of its latticed freight wagons.

If the design of the wagons is cleared by the CTSA, Eurotunnel will be free to resume freight services in mid-June as planned. Analysts do not expect the authority to rule against the design of the freight wagons -- a move which would be a huge setback for Eurotunnel resulting in a hefty bill for redesign and further loss of freight revenue.

Eurotunnel shut down its freight services after last November's blaze which resulted in lorry drivers being taken to hospital for treatment. Eurotunnel's own internal inquiry cleared its equipment of any fault but admitted to "avoidable delays" in tackling the fire.

But the Kent Fire Brigade, involved in the CTSA inquiry, has been loud in its criticism of the design of Eurotunnel's freight wagons -- claiming their lattice-work design created a blow-torch effect once the fire was underway. It has argued for a re-design.

The outcome of the CTSA report will be crucial not just to getting services back on track but also to getting shareholders' and banking syndicate approval for Eurotunnel's debt restructuring which was recently approved by the lead lending banks.
The prospectus for the debt deal is due to go out to shareholders before the end of May making a positive CTSA report integral to the company's survival.
